view='te': triple target encoding (auto/10/100) on 8 keys (3 cat cols + 5 income/commute/age smoothing keys), no digits/flags/counts. First run scored 0.94610, this OOF is from the second run (0.94607) -- run-to-run noise from LightGBM's multithreaded nondeterminism.

view='raw': only 14 original columns + 2 ratios, single-smoothing TE on the 3 cat cols. Much weaker than full (0.94617) or te (0.94607) -- 0.0029 gap, bigger than the MLP's 0.0017 gap that already scored 0 weight in the blend. Likely too weak to help regardless of decorrelation, per the established strength-vs-correlation tradeoff.

view='te' + 13 org_mean features (real-dataset per-value buy rate, from EV_Adoption_and_Range_Anxiety_Dataset.csv). Essentially identical to plain te (0.94607/0.94610) -- org_mean adds nothing on top of triple TE, likely redundant signal. Idea from public notebook najiama/pure-lgbm-model-cv-0-94607-lb-0-94638, whose own gain came from smooth-keys+triple-TE (already in our 'te' view), not org_mean itself.

4-way rank blend: catboost_tuned + lgbm + lgbm_te + lgbm_te_org. lgbm_te/lgbm_te_org Spearman 0.99900 -- near-duplicate models, adds essentially nothing over the 3-way blend (0.946225, +0.000008). Confirms the ceiling: full run of feature-view experimentation (full/te/te_org/raw) plus blending moved OOF from single-model 0.94617 to 0.946233, a total gain of +0.000063 -- within noise.

full view (58 feats) + 5 neighbourhood-window income/commute encodings (radii 50/500/5000 and 2/10, cross-fitted). Identical to plain full view (0.94617) to 5 decimals -- our existing digit features + multi-scale smooth-key TE already capture the smooth income/commute relationship the window encoding targets, so adding it changes nothing. Inspired by a public notebook (LB 0.94646) that combines window encoding with ~15 other feature families (orig-row concatenation into training, generator-lift ratios, bigrams, groupby deviations) -- this isolated test shows window encoding alone is not what drives their gain; it must be the combination.

full view (58 feats) + joint target encoding of concern_x_anxiety, concern_x_subsidy, attitude_trigram. No improvement over plain full (0.94617); slightly lower, within noise. Likely explanation: boosting composes signal across ~1000+ trees even with colsample_bytree=0.3, so the model already had ample chances to see all 3 columns together over many trees -- an explicit joint key wasn't necessary. Note: the public notebook that inspired this actually encoded the *lift ratio* (synthetic pool freq / original-dataset freq) of the trigram, not the trigram's raw target rate directly -- a different, unreplicated mechanism that this test does not rule out.

full view (58 feats) + ~9,000 original real rows concatenated into each fold's training set (independent 10-fold split of the 10k original dataset). Slightly worse than plain full (0.94617), not better. Matches the pre-registered expectation: our own buy_score calibration check already showed the synthetic data follows the same conditional relationship as the real data (predicted vs actual buy rate matched almost exactly), so the 600k+ synthetic rows already contain the same information as the 9k real rows, at much lower variance -- concatenating a small slice of real rows adds no correction, just noise from a slightly different training distribution per fold.

Plain sklearn LogisticRegression on the same 58-feature full view as LightGBM (scaled, TE fit per fold). Motivated by the recovered generator formula being linear + threshold, and by community mentions that logistic regression reveals the real data's smooth curve. Ran entirely locally (fast, no GPU needed). OOF 0.94412 -- meaningfully below LightGBM (0.94617) and CatBoost (0.94609) but far above the raw buy_score formula alone (0.938), showing feature engineering already linearized most of the signal. Spearman with lgbm: 0.9875 (similar to MLP's 0.987), gap 0.002 (larger than MLP's 0.0017) -- optimal blend weight ~0, same story as MLP: decorrelation not enough to offset the strength gap.
